T.label: Primary Tumor (combined clinical + pathological; prefix encodes which)

categories.description: Clinical: primary tumor cannot be assessed
Clinical: no evidence of primary tumor
Clinical: clinically inapparent tumor that is not palpable (parent for cT1a/b/c)
Clinical: tumor incidental histologic finding in 5% or less of tissue resected
Clinical: tumor incidental histologic finding in more than 5% of tissue resected
Clinical: tumor identified by needle biopsy in one or both sides, but not palpable
Clinical: tumor palpable and confined within prostate (parent for cT2a/b/c)
Clinical: tumor involves one-half of one side or less
Clinical: tumor involves more than one-half of one side but not both sides
Clinical: extraprostatic tumor that is not fixed or does not invade adjacent structures (parent for cT3a/b)
Clinical: tumor is fixed or invades adjacent structures other than seminal vesicles (external sphincter, rectum, bladder, levator muscles, pelvic wall)
Pathological: organ confined (NOTE: there is no pT1)
Pathological: extraprostatic extension (unilateral or bilateral) or microscopic invasion of bladder neck
Pathological: tumor is fixed or invades adjacent structures other than seminal vesicles

notes.no_pt1: There is no pathological T1 classification.
notes.r1: Positive surgical margin should be indicated by an R1 descriptor (residual microscopic disease).

categories.description: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
Other site(s) with or without bone disease

notes.most_advanced: When more than one site of metastasis is present, the most advanced category is used. M1c is most advanced.

notes.matching: Prostate AJCC 8 encodes classification in the T-value prefix (cT/pT); this Classification axis is kept for parity with other organ models and is not used by the rule lookup.

notes.missing: When either PSA or Grade Group is unavailable, grouping should be determined by T category and/or whichever of PSA/GG is available. Source does not define a discrete 'unknown PSA' band.
